ingestionHazardClasses.name: Button / Coin Lithium Batteries (CR2032, LR44)
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Digital kitchen food scales, meat thermometers, electronic kitchen timers, novelty illuminated drink stirrers, talking recipe books.
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: When lodged in the moist esophagus, an electrical circuit is completed with mucosal fluids. Direct electric current hydrolyzes tissue water into hydroxide ions (OH-), producing severe localized alkaline burns (pH climbs to 13-14 within 15 minutes). This causes liquefactive necrosis that can erode into the thoracic aorta (causing fatal exsanguination) or trachea within 2 hours.
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: IF CHILD IS OVER 12 MONTHS OLD AND ABLE TO SWALLOW: Administer 2 teaspoons (10 mL) of pure commercial honey immediately, and repeat every 10 minutes (up to 6 doses) while en route to Pediatric Emergency Department. Honey coats the battery, slows hydroxide ion generation, and buffers localized alkaline tissue erosion. DO NOT DELAY hospital transport to obtain honey. DO NOT induce vomiting. DO NOT give other food or liquids.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: NEVER induce vomiting. DO NOT administer honey to infants under 12 months (risk of infant botulism). Do not give milk, water, or citrus juices.
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Sudden refusal to eat/drink, persistent drooling, chest discomfort, stridor, coughing up dark blood or coffee-ground emesis.
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: Over 3,500 button battery ingestions reported annually in the US; 60% involve children under 6. Esophageal perforation risk escalates exponentially when diameter >= 20mm (CR2032).

ingestionHazardClasses.name: Single-Dose Dishwasher Detergent Pods / Pacs
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Countertop or under-sink dishwasher pod storage tubs, brightly colored liquid-gel packets.
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: Pods contain highly concentrated alkaline surfactants (pH 10.5-11.5), ethoxylated alcohols, and enzymes encased in water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) film. When bitten, the pod ruptures under pressure, projecting concentrated fluid into the pharynx and eyes. Surfactants cause chemical mucosal burns, severe esophageal irritation, central nervous system depression, and severe aspiration pneumonitis if foaming fluid enters the tracheobronchial tree.
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: IMMEDIATELY gently wipe mouth and rinse oral cavity with cold water or damp cloth. If detergent touched eyes or skin, flush continuously with tepid running water for at least 15 minutes. CALL POISON CONTROL (1-800-222-1222) OR 911 IMMEDIATELY. Watch breathing continuously.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: ABSOLUTELY NEVER INDUCE VOMITING! Inducing emesis causes the concentrated surfactant to foam aggressively in the esophagus and be inhaled into the lungs (aspiration pneumonitis), which can cause fatal chemical asphyxiation. Do not give raw milk or activated charcoal.
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Persistent coughing, stridor, wheezing, excessive drooling, lethargy, respiratory depression, white mucosal chemical burns.
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: Over 10,000 pediatric laundry/dishwasher pod exposures logged annually by US Poison Centers; ~85% in toddlers under age 3.

ingestionHazardClasses.name: High-Powered Rare-Earth Neodymium Magnets
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Magnetic kitchen spice jars, refrigerator novelty magnet clusters, magnetic knife racks, desk fidget balls in home kitchens.
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) rare-earth magnets exhibit extreme magnetic flux (>1.2 Tesla). When two or more magnets (or one magnet and a ferromagnetic utensil/metal object) are swallowed, they travel independently through the gastrointestinal tract and attract each other across adjacent loops of bowel. The immense pinching force causes localized pressure necrosis, bowel wall perforation, fistulas, volvulus, peritonitis, septic shock, and fatal internal bowel gangrene.
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: PROCEED IMMEDIATELY TO PEDIATRIC EMERGENCY ROOM for serial bi-plane abdominal radiographs (X-rays). Inform medical staff specifically that rare-earth neodymium magnets are suspected. Child must remain NPO (nothing by mouth: no food, no liquids). Keep child still to prevent internal bowel wall tearing.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING. Do not administer laxatives or stool softeners without direct pediatric surgical consultation. Do not perform MRI imaging before X-ray confirmation (MRI can violently yank internal magnets through bowel walls).
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Child may be completely symptom-free for the first 4-8 hours! Delayed onset of progressive abdominal pain, vomiting, fever, abdominal distension, lethargy, septic shock.
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: CPSC instituted safety standards following thousands of pediatric surgeries; multiple magnet ingestion requires exploratory laparotomy in >50% of confirmed cases.

ingestionHazardClasses.name: Caustic Oven & Heavy-Duty Degreasers / Drain Openers
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Oven cleaner aerosol sprays, lye-based drain uncloggers, caustic grill cleaner foam stored in lower kitchen cabinets.
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: Concentrated alkalis (NaOH, KOH) cause instantaneous liquefactive necrosis upon contact with mucous membranes, saponifying fats and denaturing proteins. Unlike acids which cause coagulative necrosis (forming a protective eschar), alkalis penetrate deeply into the muscularis layer of the esophagus and stomach wall, causing transmural necrosis, full esophageal perforation, mediastinitis, and long-term strictures requiring repeated esophageal dilations or colon transposition surgery.
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY. If child is conscious, alert, and able to swallow comfortably, give small sips (no more than 2-4 oz / 60-120 mL) of plain water to clear residual caustic agent from the oropharynx. If skin or eyes are exposed, flush immediately with running water for 20 minutes.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: ABSOLUTELY NEVER ATTEMPT CHEMICAL NEUTRALIZATION WITH VINEGAR, LEMON JUICE, OR ACID! Acid-base neutralization produces an intense exothermic chemical reaction (generating heat >60°C / 140°F) that inflicts devastating secondary thermal burns on already liquified esophageal tissue! NEVER induce vomiting.
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Intense oral burning, refusal to swallow, continuous drooling, hoarseness, stridor (airway swelling), hematemesis, thoracic or epigastric pain.
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: Caustic alkali ingestions represent the highest rate of surgical ICU admission and long-term disability among all household chemical exposures.

ingestionHazardClasses.name: Pure Vanilla & Baking Extracts, Cooking Spirits
ingestionHazardClasses.severity: HIGH MEDICAL RISK - PEDIATRIC HYPOGLYCEMIA & CNS DEPRESSION
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Pure vanilla extract (minimum 35% ABV by FDA 21 CFR § 169.175), almond extract, lemon oil extract, cooking sherry, high-proof liqueur.
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: Toddlers and young children metabolize ethanol differently than adults. Pediatric alcohol dehydrogenase pathways rapidly convert ethanol, halting hepatic gluconeogenesis. A single 2 oz (60 mL) bottle of pure vanilla extract contains as much ethanol as a shot and a half of 80-proof vodka. In a 12 kg (26 lb) toddler, this can trigger profound hypoglycemia (blood glucose <40 mg/dL), metabolic acidosis, hypothermia, seizures, and respiratory arrest.
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: CALL POISON CONTROL (1-800-222-1222) IMMEDIATELY with the bottle in hand to calculate exact ethanol milligrams per kilogram of child weight. If child is awake and responsive, offer a high-glucose beverage (apple juice or sugar water) to counter sudden hypoglycemia while awaiting professional instruction.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING (risk of alcohol aspiration and respiratory depression). Do not attempt home remedies or let the child 'sleep it off'.
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Stumbling or ataxia, slurred babbling, glassy eyes, hypothermia (cold clammy skin), seizures, stupor, slow or irregular shallow breathing (<12 breaths/min).
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: Extracts are frequently overlooked by parents because they are sold in grocery baking aisles, yet thousands of pediatric ethanol poisonings occur annually.

ingestionHazardClasses.name: Raw or Undercooked Red Kidney Beans (Phytohaemagglutinin)
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Uncooked dried red kidney beans, white cannellini beans, slow-cooker chili made with dry beans below 100°C (212°F).
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: Raw kidney beans contain high concentrations of the toxic glycoprotein phytohaemagglutinin (PHA: up to 70,000 hemagglutinating units per gram). As few as 4 to 5 raw beans can cause severe acute toxic gastrointestinal injury in a young child. PHA binds to carbohydrate receptors on intestinal epithelial cells, causing mucosal microvillar disruption, rapid fluid loss, and systemic cell agglutination. Note: Slow cookers operating below boiling can increase lectin toxicity up to five-fold!
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: CALL POISON CONTROL (1-800-222-1222). Note the estimated number of beans ingested and whether raw or soaked. Prevent pediatric dehydration by providing small sips of oral rehydration solution (Pedialyte) once acute vomiting subsides under medical guidance.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: DO NOT administer OTC anti-diarrheal or anti-emetic medications without pediatric physician authorization. Do not induce vomiting mechanically.
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Sudden onset (within 1-3 hours) of violent projectile vomiting, severe cramping, and explosive diarrhea leading to rapid pediatric dehydration.
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: FDA Food Safety Handbook highlights PHA poisoning from un-boiled dry beans as one of the most common kitchen plant toxin emergencies.

ingestionHazardClasses.name: Concentrated Essential Oils, Clove & Peppermint Extracts
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Food-grade essential oils (peppermint, cinnamon, clove / eugenol, tea tree, wintergreen / methyl salicylate) kept in spice racks or cabinets.
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: Concentrated essential oils are not water-soluble and possess extreme lipophilicity. Oil of wintergreen contains 98% methyl salicylate (1 teaspoon equals ~21 adult aspirin tablets!). Clove oil contains eugenol, which is directly cytotoxic to hepatocytes (liver necrosis). Peppermint/eucalyptus vapors cause reflex glottic spasm, and oil aspiration into the lungs causes fatal hydrocarbon-like lipoid chemical pneumonitis.
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: CALL POISON CONTROL (1-800-222-1222) OR 911 IMMEDIATELY. Have the exact bottle and brand name available. Wipe child's face and lips with cool damp cloth.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING! Regurgitating lipophilic essential oils dramatically multiplies the risk of pulmonary aspiration and asphyxiation. DO NOT give milk or vegetable oil (lipids enhance systemic gastrointestinal absorption!).
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Persistent coughing, choking, ataxia, unusual euphoria followed by sudden lethargy, hyperventilation, seizures, burns around the mouth.
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: Essential oil exposures in children under 5 have surged >100% over the last decade with the popularity of home diffuser and culinary oils.

ingestionHazardClasses.name: Boiling Kettle / Slow Cooker / Hot Oil Scald Hazard
ingestionHazardClasses.commonSources: Overhanging kettle power cords, slow cookers on counter edges, boiling pasta pots on front stove burners, hot cooking grease.
ingestionHazardClasses.mechanismOfInjury: Toddler skin is thin and delicate; water at 60°C (140°F) inflicts full-thickness, third-degree burns in just 3 seconds, and at 68°C (155°F) in under 1 second. Pulling dangling cords or reaching counter edges spills liters of near-boiling liquid directly onto the child's head, neck, face, and chest, causing extensive scald trauma, hypovolemic shock, and airway edema.
ingestionHazardClasses.immediateTriageProtocol: IMMEDIATELY CALL 911. Cool the burned area with cool (not ice-cold) running tap water for 10-20 minutes. Remove wet, soaked clothing gently unless adhered to the skin. Cover with clean, dry, non-adherent sterile dressing or clean plastic wrap. Keep child warm to prevent hypothermia.
ingestionHazardClasses.contraindications: NEVER apply ice, ice water, butter, mayonnaise, flour, or ointments (ice causes vasoconstriction and worsens tissue ischemia; food items introduce severe bacterial infections). Do not pop burn blisters.
ingestionHazardClasses.clinicalRedFlags: Blistering, white or charred leather-like skin, shock (pale skin, rapid shallow breathing, weak pulse, apathy), burns affecting face, hands, feet, or genitals.
ingestionHazardClasses.aapccData: Over 300 children are treated in US emergency rooms every day for scald and burn injuries; 70% of scalds occur in domestic kitchens.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: Are lower under-sink and base cabinets containing cleaning chemicals, dishwasher pods, and drain cleaners secured with child-resistant safety latches?

options.label: Yes - Secured with magnetic or dual-latch childproof locks (Tested child-resistant)
Partial - Some standard push-tab latches (Toddler can pry open with force)
No - Completely unlocked or chemicals stored directly on lower cabinet floors

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Install magnetic safety locks (tested to CPSC child resistance standards) on all base cabinets or relocate all chemicals to upper wall cabinets >= 5 feet (1.5 m) high.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: Where are single-dose dishwasher detergent pods / pacs stored in your kitchen?

options.label: High closed cabinet (>5 feet up) in original child-deterrent packaging
Under the kitchen sink with a child lock installed
On countertop, near dishwasher, or in clear decorative glass jars

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Never store detergent pods in clear jars or on countertops. Keep pods in original opaque, child-deterrent bags/boxes locked in an upper wall cabinet.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: Do kitchen food scales, meat thermometers, and digital timers have screw-secured battery compartments?

options.label: Yes - All coin battery compartments require a screwdriver or dual-action tool to open
Some do; spare button batteries are kept in high, taped drawers
Snap-fit / loose battery covers, or spare button batteries in accessible kitchen junk drawers

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Audit all digital kitchen electronics for compliant screw-locked battery compartments under Reese's Law (16 CFR Part 1263). Lock spare coin cells in a high security container.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: Are there high-powered rare-earth neodymium magnets or small decorative magnet clusters on your refrigerator or lower surfaces?

options.label: No - Only large one-piece sheet magnets (>1.75 inch diameter) or zero magnets in reach
Magnets are placed above child eye level (>4 feet), but can be knocked down with broom/chair
Small neodymium magnet clips, loose magnetic marbles, or small souvenir magnets within child reach

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Completely remove all small or high-powered rare-earth magnets from the kitchen. Toddlers climb on chairs or open freezer drawers to reach shiny magnetic objects.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: How are pots and pans positioned on your cooktop when cooking with children present?

options.label: Always rear burners only, with pot handles turned inward towards the back wall
Front burners used occasionally, but handles are kept turned inward
Front burners used with handles protruding outward over the stove edge

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Cook exclusively on back burners when toddlers are in the home. Install stove knob safety covers and keep all pan handles angled strictly toward the wall.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: Is the child-lock feature activated on your dishwasher, oven door, and induction cooktop?

options.label: Yes - All electronic control lockouts and mechanical oven latch locks are active
Dishwasher locked, but oven door can be pulled open by a toddler
No child lockouts active; appliances can be opened or turned on with one touch

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Engage digital control lockout (hold lock button 3 seconds) on dishwashers to prevent toddlers opening hot, pod-soiled pre-wash cycles. Install mechanical oven latches.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: How are chef knives, kitchen shears, and mandoline slicers stored?

options.label: In a safety-latched high drawer, in-drawer sheath, or high magnetic strip far out of reach
In a countertop wood knife block near the counter edge
Loose in an unlocked lower kitchen drawer or drying on the sink rack

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Move heavy knife blocks against the back wall or inside high cabinets. Toddlers can pull down countertop knife blocks or grab blades from unlocked utensil drawers.

childproofingAuditChecklist.question: Where are pure vanilla extracts (35% alcohol), flavorings, food coloring, and raw dry kidney beans stored?

options.label: High closed pantry or spice cabinet (>5 feet up) with doors kept latched
Middle spice rack, occasionally accessible by climbing on kitchen chairs
Low open spice pull-out drawer or pantry shelf near the floor

childproofingAuditChecklist.recommendation: Store pure baking extracts alongside medications and chemicals in elevated pantry shelves. Remember that 2 oz of vanilla extract has the ethanol equivalent of 1.5 vodka shots.

tier1_critical.rationale: High probability of irreversible chemical tissue liquefaction, acute airway obstruction, cardiac arrhythmia, or intestinal perforation within 1-2 hours.

tier2_high.hospitalTransport: Call Poison Control Immediately (1-800-222-1222) / ER Evaluation
tier2_high.rationale: Significant metabolic or respiratory toxicity (hypoglycemia, chemical pneumonitis, severe mucosal burns) requiring urgent clinical monitoring.

tier3_moderate.rationale: Gastrointestinal distress, mucosal irritation, or lectin poisoning requiring hydration management and observation.
